planting.note: Plant in fast-draining, sandy, acidic soil in full sun; tough buckthorn is a dune and coastal-scrub native that resents any soil richness or extra moisture beyond what rainfall provides.

directions: Tough buckthorn is a spiny, evergreen shrub to small tree of stabilized coastal dunes, maritime forests, and sandy scrub from South Carolina south through Florida and west along the Gulf to Louisiana, tolerating salt spray and blowing sand better than most woody natives. Stiff, thorn-tipped branches carry small, leathery, dark green leaves with a silvery-to-rusty pubescent underside, a texture that distinguishes it from the more uniformly hairy foliage of gum bumelia and the more restricted, non-coastal range of Alachua buckthorn. Small clustered white flowers draw a wide range of pollinators in late summer, followed by small black drupes that persist into fall and feed birds through the lean months. Because it is so intolerant of rich or consistently moist soil, plant it only in genuinely lean, sandy, sharply draining ground and skip supplemental fertilizer entirely.
